name: Equatorial Guinea
summary: Green, white and red horizontal bands with a blue triangle at the hoist and the coat of arms in the centre: a silk-cotton tree under six stars, with the motto 'Unidad, Paz, Justicia'.
origin: The flag was adopted at independence from Spain on 12 October 1968. Under the dictator Francisco Macías Nguema (1972–1979) the arms were replaced with a symbol including a cockerel, tools and a sword.
After Macías was overthrown in 1979, the original coat of arms was restored.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Natural resources, agriculture and the jungle.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sea that connects the mainland and the islands.

symbols.name: Silk-cotton tree
symbols.description: A ceiba (God tree) in a silver shield.
symbols.meaning: The tree under which a treaty between local ruler Bonkoro and Spain was said to be signed.

symbols.name: Six stars
symbols.description: Six yellow six-pointed stars above the shield.
symbols.meaning: The mainland and the five main islands.

facts: It is the only African country with Spanish as an official language.
Its capital, Malabo, is on the island of Bioko, not the mainland.
The six stars stand for Río Muni, Bioko, Annobón, Corisco, Elobey Grande and Elobey Chico.
clues: Green, white and red bands with a blue hoist triangle and a tree under six stars.
Its six stars are the mainland and five islands.
